subject: [PATCH] eth: bnxt: fix the agg page pool ring size on 64K-page kernels

reviews.author: Björn Töpel
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the divisor in the agg_size_fac calculation should be max(PAGE_SIZE, rx_page_size) / rx_page_size to correctly account for buffer allocation sizes and page pool ring size on 64K-page kernels.
reviews.raw_body:
Yeah, this was mostly me thinking out loud! :-)

Thanks for doing the change! The patch above looks good, feel free to
add:

Reviewed-by: Björn Töpel <bjorn@kernel.org>


Cheers,
Björn

2026-11-26.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the Broadcom NIC driver (bnxt) that affects the size of the aggregate page pool recycle ring on 64K-page kernels. The issue arises from incorrect calculation of the fill level, which is divided by the number of buffers per allocation instead of just the buffer size. This leads to under-sized rings and reduced memory efficiency. The patch corrects this by dividing the fill level by the maximum of the page size and the rx_page_size, ensuring that the ring size is correctly calculated for both 64K-page kernels and systems with larger buffer sizes.
